- `op_table.rs` — the op table as DATA (road map 7's D3): one `OpRow` per
  op and one `Argument` per argument — its name, its `Kind` (`Kind::Output`
  for `set_canvas`'s dynamic range, `Kind::Blending` for its blending),
  whether the
  decoder requires it and, for the few that have one, its `Bound` — and
  `OP_NAMES` as a projection of it, re-exported by
  `edit.rs` so no caller moved. The rows (`OP_TABLE`) and `OP_NAMES` live in
  `op_rows.rs` (road map "creator-jobs" CJ0b's toll T1, a pure move),
  re-exported by `op_table.rs` so every `op_table::` path holds; an op's row
  is added there, and the four builders `req`, `opt`, `within` and `op` are
  `pub(crate)` for it. A published interface, where the `Op` enum
  and the dispatch are its implementation. Its one reader in the crate is
  `op_schema.rs`, which carries the rows out through the FFI; the APP's
  reader is every one of the sixty-nine op tools in the agent catalog,
  which print these rows instead of restating them. **A `Bound` is
  published only where the core REFUSES outside it** — `set_canvas`'s two
  dimensions, sourced from `edit_canvas.rs`'s own constants, and
  `add_graphic_clip`'s `width` and `height`, from `model_graphic.rs`'s, never
  retyped — and never where it CLAMPS, which is the app's to say in its
  prose. A row holds no prose, no semantics and no default spelled twice;
  `Kind` is closed (thirty kinds — `reframe_clip` added `Follow` (its members end `layout`,
  `speaker`, `center`, `fit`, `keep`),
  `WhereEmpty` and `Subjects`, the last a caller-authored object declared
  and closed at every level; `switch_layout` added `Layout`,
  `LayoutShape`, `Corner` and `Point`, `[f64; 2]`; `Texts`, a list of strings, is
  `set_action_end`'s `off`), carries each vocabulary's members, and has exactly ONE
  kind per answer serde gives, because a distinction the
  decoder cannot see is one no test could prove. Nothing here is the
  authority — the enum's fields are, and `core/tests/op_table.rs` proves
  every row by asking the decoder. Capped at 400 lines like any new module:
  it does NOT inherit `edit.rs`'s table exemption.
- `op_schema.rs` — `op_table.rs` written as JSON Schema, which is what
  `rc_op_schemas` publishes (road map 7's D3·2): one object per op, its
  properties the arguments and its `required` the ones the decoder will not
  do without. **The match over `Kind` is exhaustive** — a kind added to the
  table does not compile until this says what JSON it is — and it is a
  module of its own because a row changes when an OP does and this changes
  when the published DIALECT does. It says nothing about what an argument is
  FOR (the catalog's prose), nothing about what a patch may CARRY
  (`Kind::Object` is an object with no properties; D1 left the core the one
  validator of that), and nothing about `additionalProperties` on an op,
  because the catalog merges `project` and `scope` in afterwards. Tested
  through the FFI in `core/tests/op_schemas.rs`.
- `scope.rs` — editing INSIDE a nest: the envelope's `scope` key. Builds a
  VIEW project from the nest (its tracks and clips at top level, its frozen
  size as the canvas, the parent's rate, media, `next_id` and nests, no
  markers), applies the op to it UNCHANGED, merges back. So `Project::clip`
  keeps its one meaning and no op has a nest-aware branch. Three things are
  counter-intuitive and measured: the scoped nest's own row stays in the view
  with its tracks and clips EMPTIED (removing it dangles every other nest's
  reference; leaving it whole doubles every id under `validate`); the nests
  write-back is union first, orphans after; and **a scoped apply has a wider
  `Err` arm than any unscoped op** — `check_caps` and `check_nesting` are
  document-wide and run on the MERGED parent, so an op valid inside the nest
  can still return `Err`. `refused_inside` is an EXHAUSTIVE match over every
  op, so a new op does not compile until it is classified; `set_media_cursor`
  is refused inside like `set_media_speech` (twelve ops in all, `edit.rs`'s
  module doc). The READ half is
  `rc_project_scoped` in `ffi.rs`, which calls the same `scoped_view`.
- `edit_graphic.rs` — `add_graphic_clip` and `set_graphic`: every argument
  checked through `model_graphic.rs` BEFORE `edit_described.rs`'s
  `add_described_clip` (`pub(crate)`, with `Described`) places the clip, so

  `set_graphic`'s patch reader takes `name`, `width`, `height`, `length`,

  an action on the clip names stores the schema's default (G-34 (d)).

  exactly the clip's speed (spec §11, #22 and D4-2 to D4-5); the other
  writers are `edit_canvas.rs`'s `resnap`, `edit_paste.rs`'s two loops,

- `edit_speed_profile.rs` — what a rate edit scales (SR-19 (a), (b)), a pure
  move out of `edit_clip_timing.rs` (road map creator-jobs CU9a's toll), all
  `pub(crate)`.
  - `profile_factors` (None on every constant clip).
  - `scaled_profile`: scales the base, every end rate and every speed span.

    also uses. It writes an unclamped rate as asked, holds the window, then
    re-clamps the other actions into the held duration through
    `resnap_actions`.
  - `rescale_actions`: actions keep their clip-relative fraction.
  - Shared by `set_speed`, `rate_stretch` and `retime_range`.
- `edit_retime.rs` — `retime_range` (road map creator-jobs CU9a, spec §11
  CU-90).
  - The range `[from, to)` is played at `rate` on every unlocked track.
  - Both bounds are cut by `split_under_playhead`. The pieces (unlocked
    clips wholly inside) are found before `shift_clips` moves everything at
    or after `to` by `to′ − to`, partners included.
  - Each piece starts at `f(s)` and lasts `f(e) − f(s)`, where
    `f(t) = snapped(from + round((t − from) ÷ rate))`: a constant media
    piece at speed × rate, held by `duration_resnapped`; a ramp by
    `scaled_profile`; every other kind scaled, a graphic keeping its
    `length`.
  - Markers inside map through `f`; markers after move with the shift. Two
    markers landing on one tick are refused, never dropped. A scoped view

    identity once in range. AU-94's sentence comes through `edit_link.rs`'s

- `edit_pieces.rs` — `copy_pieces` (road map "creator-jobs" SW1, spec §11

  another track at the same times. `Err` for an unknown clip, then track;
  each pair ordered and snapped, an empty one dropped (none left an
  identity), sorted; then the refusals in order — a nest clip, a range
  outside the clip, overlapping ranges (touching allowed), a locked
  destination (`locked_track`), a destination holding a clip (the first by

- `edit_detach.rs` — `detach_audio` and `set_enabled`, a clip's video and

- `edit_fit.rs` — `fit_scale` and `fill_scale` (Fit is a RESCUE for oversized

- `edit_link.rs` — linked pairs (format 28, spec §11 AU-90…AU-96): Detach

  caller order and check old tracks before destination tracks; additions

  one draft and call `finish_placement`, which mints gained transitions on

  rule they all obey. `state_patch` and `narrow_to` are `pub(crate)`:

## Rules

**Modules and size.** New feature area = new module with its own
`impl Project` block. Soft cap ~600 lines; needing a new `// ---- name --`
banner section is the signal to split. Every module keeps a `//!` doc;
numeric and algorithmic choices get prose "why" comments. **A file at the cap
gives something up BEFORE it takes anything on**: the cut is a PURE MOVE,
landed and gated alone, so the feature's diff is attributable; budget the cut
against the pessimistic number, because an estimate here has run about two
thirds of the truth. Over the cap today and known debt, not licence:
`edit.rs`, whose
standing exemption is that its module doc IS the op table's semantics half
(the cut there, if ever forced, is the `Op` enum into an `edit_ops.rs`, and
never in the same phase as a feature). The current list is `wc -l`; named
seams are in `designs/adr/core-file-history.md` "Named next cuts".

**Dependencies.** `serde` and `serde_json` (the JSON the FFI speaks),
`tiny_http` (the agent's socket), and `serde_path_to_error`, which is there
so a patch refusal names the path to what only the type can refuse (a
misspelt variant, a `null` a required field cannot take), where serde alone
names only the value. `graphic` (the path crate `../graphic`, road map
10's motion-graphics engine), named by `ffi_graphic.rs` alone. It enables
`serde_json`'s `preserve_order`, and a feature is unified across a path
dependency, so the core's `serde_json` has it too; `Cargo.toml` spells it
out. `svgtypes` 0.16.1 (usvg's own pin, already in the lock) for its
named-colour table only, so a stored name agrees with what usvg draws
(`model_color.rs`). `sha2` for the `.fjgraphic` manifest's checksums
(G-46; also `graphic_ffi.rs`'s revision oracle).

**One implementation per algorithm.** Before writing time math, find the
existing implementation and route through it. Shared constants have exactly
one home (`TIMESCALE` in `time.rs`; `RC_*` caps in `format.rs`; the
inspector's bounds in `props_check.rs`).

**Purity.** Every edit takes `&self` and returns a new value — internally
clone-then-mutate. An op that would change nothing returns
`Outcome::Identity`, never an identical copy: an identical copy registers a
phantom undo step in the app.

**Errors.** Every edit answers `Result<Outcome, String>` — three arms and
one tier, no error enum. `Outcome::Applied` = the new project;
`Outcome::Identity` = the op is valid and nothing needed to change;
`Outcome::Refused(String)` = a rule declined it, carrying the rule's OWN
sentence rather than a second one written at the call site; `Err(String)` =
invalid arguments, unknown ids, parse failures — lowercase messages naming
the offending value. A refusal is not an error tier: both middle arms leave
the project untouched and register no undo step. No input may panic. FFI
mapping (`ffi_edit.rs`): `Applied` → a new handle; `Identity` → NULL with
neither channel written; `Refused` → NULL with the sentence through
`reason_out`; `Err` → NULL with the message through `err_out`; caught panic
→ `"internal error: <what>"`. The two channels are never both written.

**Times.** Every tick value that reaches the model is snapped to the
document's frame grid before it is stored (`time::snap_to_frame`). Never
store a sub-frame time. Where a range check names the value, the check runs
on what the CALLER sent and the snap follows it, so a refusal never names a
number the door rounded to (`props_check.rs`, `edit_props.rs`'s
`snap_motion` / `snap_animation`). The one family that is deliberately NOT
on the grid is the audio ramps — `audio.fade_in` / `fade_out`, the duck's
and the compressor's attack and release — because they are envelope lengths
sampled at the audio rate, not positions in the picture, and quantising them
to a video frame would round a 10 ms attack to nothing. The other is a SHIFT
(spec §11 #42): an op that moves several clips — the ripples, `close_gap`,
`insert_time`, `move_clip` — moves them all by ONE delta so abutments stay
exact, and at a rate whose frame is not a whole number of ticks (7 fps) a
moved start may sit a tick off the grid; a canvas rate change re-snaps (D7-3).

**FFI exports.** Every export: `#[no_mangle] pub unsafe extern "C"`, a `///`
comment restating the header contract, a `/// # Safety` paragraph, NULL
tolerance first, narrow `unsafe {}` blocks. Route through the shared helpers
in `ffi_util.rs` — a freshly hand-rolled `catch_unwind` is a review flag.
Export names mirror the Rust method exactly.

**Format changes.** Any change to persisted project state bumps
`RC_FORMAT_VERSION` in `format.rs` **and** the `#define` in
`core/include/framejob_core.h`; the reader must keep accepting every prior
version; the writer enforces the reader's caps. A bump whose new fields all
carry a serde default needs no migrate step (versions 3 through 15 have none;
15's one step only renumbers the branch's 1015)
but still bumps, because unknown keys are ignored at every level by design
and an older build would otherwise open the file, drop the new fields on read
and write the loss back on the next save; a bump that changes a field's
SHAPE adds a step at the migration hook (`migrate_1_to_2`). Each bump gets a
`schema_vN.rs` test that opens the previous versions' fixtures and reads the
new keys' ORDER off the written text, since a parsed `Value` sorts them.
**Nothing that checks the version writes the current number as a
literal**, so a bump edits `format.rs` (and `format_history.rs`'s paragraph)
and the header and no test or proof:
- The "one past the current version, refused" tests in
  `core/tests/schema_v3.rs` and `core/tests/model_tests.rs` compute
  `RC_FORMAT_VERSION + 1` and assert the refusal's whole message with
  both numbers.
- `schema_v3.rs`'s `the_header_states_the_same_format_version_as_the_core`
  holds the header's `#define` to `format.rs`'s constant, so a bump that
  moves only one of them fails `make test`.
- The schema tests' and `model_tests.rs`'s `/version` assertions read
  `RC_FORMAT_VERSION`; `schema_v10.rs`'s byte-for-byte round trips rewrite
  the fixture's version line through its `current()` helper.
- The proof scripts (`tools/proof/*_proof.py`) read the HEADER's number
  through a `format_version()` helper. `phase9`'s "one past" fixture is
  `format_version() + 1`, and its every-version loop runs up to the current
  version. A proof that expected a literal would fail weeks later, in
  someone else's session, with nothing pointing at the bump.

A fixture's own version (`e2_proof.py`'s `VERSION = 8`, a
`schema_vN.rs`'s older files) is a literal on purpose. One claim still
moves with the schema rather than the number: when a bump appends a key to
the video object, `schema_v4.rs`'s text assertion about what follows
`obscure` fails in `make test` and names the new neighbour.

**Tests.** All tests are black-box in `core/tests/` (no `#[cfg(test)]` in
`src/`), exercised **through the FFI** wherever possible, and verified
against independently written oracles — never golden files. Shared helpers
live in `tests/common/` (`content` / `contents` — "the same clips, ids
aside" — is the one spelling of that comparison, used by `nest`'s identity
claim and `scope`'s oracle alike); new feature area = new test file. Every
new export gets at least one test plus inclusion in the null-safety sweep.
Finish Rust work with `cargo fmt` and a clean `make lint`.

governs a module now.

## Module map

- `lib.rs` — module declarations and re-exports only. No implementation code.
- `model.rs` — the spec §5.2 SHAPE: the project, its clips, sources,
  actions, markers and nests (a track is `model_track.rs` and the media
  types `model_media.rs`, both re-exported), with
  the serde defaults that say what an absent key means. The struct field

- `model_track.rs` — a track (`Track`, spec §5.2's `tracks[]` and a nest's),
  moved out of `model.rs` whole (road map "audio" AP10's toll T1) and
  re-exported by it; the track vocabulary's new keys land here: format 35's
  `volume` (0…`TRACK_VOLUME_MAX`, 4, written only when not 1) and `pan`

  `compressor` and `limiter` (the clip's `model_audio.rs` types, after `pan`,

  spec §5.2's `media[]`), moved out of `model.rs` whole (road map

- `model_props.rs` — the schema's VOCABULARY: the per-clip property types
  (`VideoProps`, `Crop`, `Shadow`, `ColorAdjust`, `Chroma`, `Filter`,
  `Reflection`, `BlendMode`) and their defaults (the audio group's are
  `model_audio.rs`'s), re-exported whole by `model.rs` so every
  `crate::model::X` path holds. **`BlendMode`'s, `ObscureKind`'s and
  `TrackMatte`'s declaration ORDER are shader discriminants** (`ProjectSnapshot.swift` and

  never reorder. `Normal` is 0 with no `+1`, so a zeroed uniform block, an

## Rules

**Modules and size.** New feature area = new module with its own
`impl Project` block. Soft cap ~600 lines; needing a new `// ---- name --`
banner section is the signal to split. Every module keeps a `//!` doc;
numeric and algorithmic choices get prose "why" comments. **A file at the cap
gives something up BEFORE it takes anything on**: the cut is a PURE MOVE,
landed and gated alone, so the feature's diff is attributable; budget the cut
against the pessimistic number, because an estimate here has run about two
thirds of the truth. Over the cap today and known debt, not licence:
`edit.rs`, whose
standing exemption is that its module doc IS the op table's semantics half
(the cut there, if ever forced, is the `Op` enum into an `edit_ops.rs`, and
never in the same phase as a feature). The current list is `wc -l`; named
seams are in `designs/adr/core-file-history.md` "Named next cuts".

**Dependencies.** `serde` and `serde_json` (the JSON the FFI speaks),
`tiny_http` (the agent's socket), and `serde_path_to_error`, which is there
so a patch refusal names the path to what only the type can refuse (a
misspelt variant, a `null` a required field cannot take), where serde alone
names only the value. `graphic` (the path crate `../graphic`, road map
10's motion-graphics engine), named by `ffi_graphic.rs` alone. It enables
`serde_json`'s `preserve_order`, and a feature is unified across a path
dependency, so the core's `serde_json` has it too; `Cargo.toml` spells it
out. `svgtypes` 0.16.1 (usvg's own pin, already in the lock) for its
named-colour table only, so a stored name agrees with what usvg draws
(`model_color.rs`). `sha2` for the `.fjgraphic` manifest's checksums
(G-46; also `graphic_ffi.rs`'s revision oracle).

**One implementation per algorithm.** Before writing time math, find the
existing implementation and route through it. Shared constants have exactly
one home (`TIMESCALE` in `time.rs`; `RC_*` caps in `format.rs`; the
inspector's bounds in `props_check.rs`).

**Purity.** Every edit takes `&self` and returns a new value — internally
clone-then-mutate. An op that would change nothing returns
`Outcome::Identity`, never an identical copy: an identical copy registers a
phantom undo step in the app.

**Errors.** Every edit answers `Result<Outcome, String>` — three arms and
one tier, no error enum. `Outcome::Applied` = the new project;
`Outcome::Identity` = the op is valid and nothing needed to change;
`Outcome::Refused(String)` = a rule declined it, carrying the rule's OWN
sentence rather than a second one written at the call site; `Err(String)` =
invalid arguments, unknown ids, parse failures — lowercase messages naming
the offending value. A refusal is not an error tier: both middle arms leave
the project untouched and register no undo step. No input may panic. FFI
mapping (`ffi_edit.rs`): `Applied` → a new handle; `Identity` → NULL with
neither channel written; `Refused` → NULL with the sentence through
`reason_out`; `Err` → NULL with the message through `err_out`; caught panic
→ `"internal error: <what>"`. The two channels are never both written.

**Times.** Every tick value that reaches the model is snapped to the
document's frame grid before it is stored (`time::snap_to_frame`). Never
store a sub-frame time. Where a range check names the value, the check runs
on what the CALLER sent and the snap follows it, so a refusal never names a
number the door rounded to (`props_check.rs`, `edit_props.rs`'s
`snap_motion` / `snap_animation`). The one family that is deliberately NOT
on the grid is the audio ramps — `audio.fade_in` / `fade_out`, the duck's
and the compressor's attack and release — because they are envelope lengths
sampled at the audio rate, not positions in the picture, and quantising them
to a video frame would round a 10 ms attack to nothing. The other is a SHIFT
(spec §11 #42): an op that moves several clips — the ripples, `close_gap`,
`insert_time`, `move_clip` — moves them all by ONE delta so abutments stay
exact, and at a rate whose frame is not a whole number of ticks (7 fps) a
moved start may sit a tick off the grid; a canvas rate change re-snaps (D7-3).

**FFI exports.** Every export: `#[no_mangle] pub unsafe extern "C"`, a `///`
comment restating the header contract, a `/// # Safety` paragraph, NULL
tolerance first, narrow `unsafe {}` blocks. Route through the shared helpers
in `ffi_util.rs` — a freshly hand-rolled `catch_unwind` is a review flag.
Export names mirror the Rust method exactly.

**Format changes.** Any change to persisted project state bumps
`RC_FORMAT_VERSION` in `format.rs` **and** the `#define` in
`core/include/framejob_core.h`; the reader must keep accepting every prior
version; the writer enforces the reader's caps. A bump whose new fields all
carry a serde default needs no migrate step (versions 3 through 15 have none;
15's one step only renumbers the branch's 1015)
but still bumps, because unknown keys are ignored at every level by design
and an older build would otherwise open the file, drop the new fields on read
and write the loss back on the next save; a bump that changes a field's
SHAPE adds a step at the migration hook (`migrate_1_to_2`). Each bump gets a
`schema_vN.rs` test that opens the previous versions' fixtures and reads the
new keys' ORDER off the written text, since a parsed `Value` sorts them.
**Nothing that checks the version writes the current number as a
literal**, so a bump edits `format.rs` (and `format_history.rs`'s paragraph)
and the header and no test or proof:
- The "one past the current version, refused" tests in
  `core/tests/schema_v3.rs` and `core/tests/model_tests.rs` compute
  `RC_FORMAT_VERSION + 1` and assert the refusal's whole message with
  both numbers.
- `schema_v3.rs`'s `the_header_states_the_same_format_version_as_the_core`
  holds the header's `#define` to `format.rs`'s constant, so a bump that
  moves only one of them fails `make test`.
- The schema tests' and `model_tests.rs`'s `/version` assertions read
  `RC_FORMAT_VERSION`; `schema_v10.rs`'s byte-for-byte round trips rewrite
  the fixture's version line through its `current()` helper.
- The proof scripts (`tools/proof/*_proof.py`) read the HEADER's number
  through a `format_version()` helper. `phase9`'s "one past" fixture is
  `format_version() + 1`, and its every-version loop runs up to the current
  version. A proof that expected a literal would fail weeks later, in
  someone else's session, with nothing pointing at the bump.

A fixture's own version (`e2_proof.py`'s `VERSION = 8`, a
`schema_vN.rs`'s older files) is a literal on purpose. One claim still
moves with the schema rather than the number: when a bump appends a key to
the video object, `schema_v4.rs`'s text assertion about what follows
`obscure` fails in `make test` and names the new neighbour.

**Tests.** All tests are black-box in `core/tests/` (no `#[cfg(test)]` in
`src/`), exercised **through the FFI** wherever possible, and verified
against independently written oracles — never golden files. Shared helpers
live in `tests/common/` (`content` / `contents` — "the same clips, ids
aside" — is the one spelling of that comparison, used by `nest`'s identity
claim and `scope`'s oracle alike); new feature area = new test file. Every
new export gets at least one test plus inclusion in the null-safety sweep.
Finish Rust work with `cargo fmt` and a clean `make lint`.

</system-reminder>

1	# mcp-proxy/CLAUDE.md — the stdio MCP proxy's rules
2	
3	Applies to everything under `mcp-proxy/`, the crate that builds
4	`framejob-mcp`: the stdio MCP server bundled as
5	`Frame Job.app/Contents/Helpers/framejob-mcp`, which external MCP clients start
6	(road map 14's MC3, spec §11 MC-3, MC-4, MC-6; the record is
7	`designs/adr/roadmap-14-agent-socket.md`). Build commands are the root `CLAUDE.md`'s:
8	`make test` and `make lint` run this crate after the core and the graphics
9	engine; `project.yml`'s "Build MCP Proxy" phase builds it, copies the binary
10	into `Contents/Helpers/` and signs it `--options runtime` with no
11	entitlements, as `agent/build.sh helper` signs the assistant's helper.
12	
13	## Module map
14	
15	- `lib.rs` — `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`, the module declarations, and `run()`:
16	  the stdin loop (one `Session`, one `Output`; each line to
17	  `session::dispatch`; stdin's end exits at once without waiting for a call
18	  in flight). It also includes `core/src/mcp_versions.rs` by `#[path]` as
19	  `mcp_versions`, so the proxy and the app negotiate from ONE list.
20	- `main.rs` — `fn main() { framejob_mcp::run() }` and nothing else.
21	- `session.rs` — `dispatch` (a blank line skipped; unparsable `-32700` and a
22	  batch `-32600`, both with a null id; a notification or a response dropped
23	  and never forwarded; every request on its own thread), `Output` (stdout
24	  behind one `Mutex`: one message, one line, flushed) and `Session` (one
25	  `Mutex` over the tools last given, `check_due` and `stranded`). What is
26	  answered where: `initialize` and `ping` here, never touching the socket;
27	  `tools/list` from the app within `LIST_READ_TIMEOUT`, else the snapshot,
28	  and it never launches (MC-4); `tools/call` launches its own bundle on
29	  `Absent`; anything else forwarded when the app answers, else `-32601`. A
30	  proxy-side failure of a call is a CallToolResult with `isError: true`.
31	  The `list_changed` check compares `serde_json::Value`s, never bytes (MC1's
32	  B9). A launch that timed out STRANDS the session: its later `Absent` calls
33	  answer the stranded sentence and launch nothing. The `stranded` check and
34	  the launch are one critical section per session (`Session.launching`), so
35	  concurrent calls that found no socket launch at most once between them.
36	- `socket.rs` — `socket_path` (`RC_AGENT_SOCKET` when not empty, else
37	  `$HOME/Library/Application Support/Frame Job/Agent/agent.sock`), `is_scratch`,
38	  `reach` (`Answers`; `Absent` for `NotFound` or `ConnectionRefused`;
39	  `Unreachable` otherwise), and `post`: one `POST /mcp HTTP/1.1` with
40	  `Connection: close`, its body read by `Content-Length` or CHUNKED —
41	  `tiny_http` 0.12 chunks any body of 32 768 bytes or more, and a
42	  `tools/list` is about 240 KB.
43	- `launch.rs` — `ensure_running`: the socket's folder made if missing
44	  (`0700`), `agent.launch.lock` beside the socket taken with `File::lock`,
45	  the re-check, `/usr/bin/open` with `open_arguments` (pure: `-n -g`, and for
46	  a scratch socket `--env RC_AGENT_SOCKET=…`, `--stderr <folder>/framejob-launch.log`
47	  and `--args -ApplePersistenceIgnoreState YES`), and the 50 ms poll until the
48	  socket answers or `launch_wait()` (`RC_MCP_LAUNCH_WAIT`, else 60 s) runs out
49	  with `timeout_sentence`.
50	- `bundle.rs` — `own_bundle` (the canonicalised executable must be
51	  `<X>.app/Contents/Helpers/<name>`) and `read_snapshot`
52	  (`Contents/Resources/agent-catalog.json`, `{version: string, tools:
53	  array}`), which the build's "Write Agent Catalog" phase writes
54	  (`app/Sources/AgentCatalogSnapshot.swift`).
55	
56	## Rules
57	
58	- **stdout is protocol only.** Every other word goes to stderr, each line
59	  starting `framejob-mcp: `; never `Frame Job: `, which is the app's parity
60	  check's prefix and which every proof reads as a complaint.
61	- **`initialize`, `ping` and `tools/list` never launch Frame Job** (MC-4);
62	  `mcp_proxy_proof.py`'s X1 and its `launch-on-list` mutant hold it.
63	- **The launch lock is held until the poll ends.** Released before it, a
64	  second proxy's re-check would find nothing answering yet and launch a
65	  second instance; X4 and the `no-lock` mutant hold it. The lock statement
66	  and `tools_list`'s `let answers = …` line are each ONE anchor a mutant
67	  replaces: keep each exactly once in `src/`.
68	- **No read timeout on a forwarded call**: an `export` may take minutes.
69	  Only the session's `tools/list` passes `LIST_READ_TIMEOUT`, because the app
70	  serves one request at a time and another client's long call would hold it.
71	- **A proxy launches only its OWN bundle**, so a copy of Frame Job launches
72	  itself; outside a bundle a call answers the sentence naming the executable.
73	- `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]` stays in `lib.rs` and `main.rs`; every `src/`
74	  file stays under 400 lines.
75	- Tests are black-box in `tests/stdio.rs`, through the built binary copied
76	  into a fake bundle with a snapshot and a scratch `RC_AGENT_SOCKET`; a stub
77	  is `tiny_http`'s `Server::http_unix`. **Only a `Fixture::launchable` fake
78	  bundle may reach `ensure_running`**: its executable is a script that
79	  records its launch and exits without binding, so `/usr/bin/open` starts
80	  nothing that lasts, and its `Drop` runs `lsregister -u` on the fake bundle
81	  before removing it, because `open` registered it with LaunchServices. Any other `tools/call` from a fake bundle is made only
82	  while a stub answers. Every stdout line of every proxy must parse as
83	  JSON-RPC 2.0. The launch of the real app is proved against the built app
84	  by `tools/proof/mcp_proxy_proof.py`, never here.
85	
86	## Dependencies, and why each
87	
88	- `serde_json` 1 (no features): the JSON-RPC. Its `Map` sorts keys, which is
89	  harmless: every comparison is of values, and a forwarded answer is
90	  re-serialised as one line.
91	- Dev: `tiny_http` 0.12, the app's own transport (`core/src/agent.rs`), for
92	  the tests' stub servers, so a stub chunks exactly as the app does.
93	- `std` for everything else: the socket, the lock (`File::lock`, Rust 1.89),
94	  `open`, the threads. No async runtime.
95

1	//! The op table — every op's ARGUMENTS, as data (spec §6).
2	//!
3	//! `edit.rs` owns what an op MEANS; this module owns what an op TAKES. One
4	//! [`OpRow`] per op, in table order, and one [`Argument`] per argument: its
5	//! name, its [`Kind`] and whether the decoder requires it. Nothing else is
6	//! in a row — no prose, no semantics, and no default spelled a second time,
7	//! because a default is what an absent argument MEANS and meaning is
8	//! `edit.rs`'s doc table.
9	//!
10	//! It is a module of its own because the table is a published interface —
11	//! the tool catalog will read it rather than restate it — while the [`Op`]
12	//! enum and the sixty-four-way dispatch are the implementation of that
13	//! interface. [`OP_NAMES`] is a projection of this table and is re-exported
14	//! from `edit.rs` under its old name, so no caller anywhere moved.
15	//!
16	//! **Nothing here is the authority.** The `Op` enum's fields are, and
17	//! `core/tests/op_table.rs` proves every row against them by asking the
18	//! decoder: an argument the op does not have makes serde answer with the
19	//! arguments it does have, an omitted required one makes it answer that the
20	//! field is missing, and a value of the wrong kind makes it answer with the
21	//! kind it wanted. A row that lies fails that test.
22	//!
23	//! ### The bound
24	//!
25	//! An argument may carry a [`Bound`], and the rule for one is narrow: **a
26	//! bound the core REFUSES outside is published; a bound it CLAMPS to is
27	//! not.** A published range is a promise a caller can build a call from,
28	//! and a range that quietly corrects what it is handed would make that
29	//! promise false in the one direction a caller could not see. So
30	//! `set_canvas`'s two dimensions carry one — `edit_canvas.rs` refuses
31	//! outside 16–16384 by name — and `set_speed`'s `rate`, which refuses a
32	//! non-positive rate and then clamps to `SPEED_MIN`–`SPEED_MAX`, carries
33	//! none: the clamp is the app's to say, in the tool prose that already says
34	//! it.
35	//!
36	//! A bound is SOURCED from the constant that enforces it and never retyped
37	//! here, which is what `core/tests/op_table.rs` checks by putting each end
38	//! to the core and reading the refusal — including the numbers in it.
39	//! A refused range that is not whole numbers (`set_track`'s `volume`
40	//! 0–4 and `pan` −1–1) is stated in the tool's prose until [`Bound`]
41	//! widens.
42	//!
43	//! ### The kinds
44	//!
45	//! The vocabulary is closed and spelled the way `edit.rs`'s argument column
46	//! spelled it. **There is exactly one kind per answer the decoder can
47	//! give**, which is the rule that says how many there are: two kinds serde
48	//! refuses identically would be a distinction the table claims and no test
49	//! could prove. So [`Kind::Ticks`], [`Kind::Number`], [`Kind::Boolean`],
50	//! [`Kind::Text`], [`Kind::Texts`], [`Kind::Ids`] and [`Kind::Ranges`] are
51	//! `Ticks`, `f64`, `bool`, `String`, `Vec<String>` (`set_action_end`'s
52	//! `off` paths), `Vec<u32>` and the silence cut's `Vec<[Ticks; 2]>`, and
53	//! the nineteen named types map like this:
54	//!
55	//! - [`Kind::Id`] — `u32`: an id naming a clip, track, action, marker or
56	//!   media, and the canvas's two pixel dimensions, which are the same whole
57	//!   non-negative number to a decoder and to a schema. [`Kind::Index`] is
58	//!   `usize`, a place in the track stack, and is its own kind only because
59	//!   serde names a different type in its refusal.
60	//! - [`Kind::Color`] — `Color`, four numbers; [`Kind::FrameRate`] — `Fps`,
61	//!   two. Named rather than "a list of numbers" because their LENGTH is
62	//!   part of what serde refuses.
63	//! - [`Kind::Transition`], [`Kind::Alignment`], [`Kind::Curve`],
64	//!   [`Kind::Fit`], [`Kind::Matte`], [`Kind::Output`], [`Kind::Blending`],
65	//!   [`Kind::RampShape`] and [`Kind::FadeShape`] — `TransitionKind`,
66	//!   `TransitionAlign`, `Curve`, `ZoomFit`, `TrackMatte`, `CanvasOutput`,
67	//!   `CanvasBlending`, `RampShape`, `FadeShape`: closed
68	//!   vocabularies, each carrying its members in [`Kind::values`] rather
69	//!   than flattened to a string, because an agent
70	//!   picking a legal value out of a schema is a reason this table exists.
71	//!   [`Kind::Groups`] is `Vec<PasteGroup>`, the one vocabulary arriving
72	//!   as a list.
73	//! - [`Kind::Layout`], [`Kind::LayoutShape`] and [`Kind::Corner`] —
74	//!   `CameraLayout`, `LayoutShape`, `LayoutCorner`: `switch_layout`'s three
75	//!   closed vocabularies (spec §11 CO-60), members in [`Kind::values`].
76	//!   [`Kind::Point`] is `[f64; 2]`, its `focus`: two numbers, whose LENGTH
77	//!   serde refuses like a colour's and whose members it names as `f64`
78	//!   where a frame rate's are `u32`.
79	//! - [`Kind::Follow`] and [`Kind::WhereEmpty`] — `FramingFollow` and
80	//!   `WhereEmpty`: `reframe_clip`'s two closed vocabularies (spec §11
81	//!   VR-26; `speaker` after `layout`, VR-60), members in [`Kind::values`]. [`Kind::Subjects`] is its
82	//!   `subjects`, a caller-authored object the core declares at every level
83	//!   and reads strictly (`edit_reframe.rs`), as [`Kind::Region`] is.
84	//! - [`Kind::Region`] — `ZoomRegion`, `add_zoom_action`'s four numbers. NOT
85	//!   an opaque object: it is a caller-authored object whose members the
86	//!   core declares and refuses by name (`edit_zoom.rs`), so a later schema
87	//!   can print them.
88	//! - [`Kind::Object`] — `serde_json::Value`: a caller-authored **patch**,
89	//!   whatever the op calls it. The decoder takes ANY json here on purpose;
90	//!   deepening D1 made the core the one validator of what a patch may
91	//!   carry, and this table does not restate a word of it.
92	//!
93	//! [`Op`]: crate::edit::Op
94	
95	use Kind::*;
96	
97	/// The rows themselves and their names live in `op_rows.rs`, a file of its
98	/// own so this one stays clear of the cap; every `op_table::` path holds.
99	pub use crate::op_rows::{OP_NAMES, OP_TABLE};
100	
101	/// How many ops there are. `edit.rs`'s enum, its dispatch and this table
102	/// all have exactly this many arms.
103	pub const OP_COUNT: usize = 70;
104	
105	/// One op's row: its name, and its arguments in the order the enum declares
106	/// them — which is the order the decoder lists them back in.
107	#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
108	pub struct OpRow {
109	    pub name: &'static str,
110	    pub arguments: &'static [Argument],
111	}
112	
113	/// One named value an op takes. `required` is the absence of a serde
114	/// default on the enum's field. Optional means omission is accepted; it does
115	/// not imply that `null` is accepted. The eight defaulted plain booleans
116	/// (`add_transition.ripple`, `paste_attributes.skip_missing`, both
117	/// `with_clips` fields, `set_canvas.rescale_clips`, and the `alone` of
118	/// `trim_start`, `trim_end` and `roll`) default to false when absent and
119	/// reject null.
120	/// Other optional fields are `Option<T>` and decode absence and null alike.
121	#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
122	pub struct Argument {
123	    pub name: &'static str,
124	    pub kind: Kind,
125	    pub required: bool,
126	    /// The range the core refuses outside, for the few arguments that have
127	    /// one (the module doc's rule). `None` is the ordinary case, and it
128	    /// means the kind is the whole of what is known — never "unbounded in
129	    /// fact".
130	    pub bound: Option<Bound>,
131	}
132	
133	/// The two ends of a range an op refuses outside, as the op's own module
134	/// spells them.
135	///
136	/// Whole numbers because the one rule that qualifies today is a canvas
137	/// dimension, whose two constants are `u32`, and a bound is taken from the
138	/// constant that enforces it. An argument whose bound is not a whole number
139	/// is a widening of this type, made deliberately and proved the same way,
140	/// rather than a cast written at a call site.
141	#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
142	pub struct Bound {
143	    pub min: u32,
144	    pub max: u32,
145	}
146	
147	/// What an argument's value IS — never what it is for (spec §7.9: the core
148	/// says what an argument is, the app says what it is for).
149	#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
150	pub enum Kind {
151	    Ticks,
152	    Id,
153	    Index,
154	    Ids,
155	    Ranges,
156	    Number,
157	    Boolean,
158	    Text,
159	    Texts,
160	    Object,
161	    Color,
162	    FrameRate,
163	    Transition,
164	    Alignment,
165	    Curve,
166	    Fit,
167	    Region,
168	    Groups,
169	    Matte,
170	    Output,
171	    Blending,
172	    RampShape,
173	    FadeShape,
174	    Layout,

240	pub(crate) const fn req(name: &'static str, kind: Kind) -> Argument {
241	    Argument {
242	        name,
243	        kind,
244	        required: true,
245	        bound: None,
246	    }

253	        kind,

263	        bound: Some(Bound { min, max }),
264	        ..argument
265	    }

# app/CLAUDE.md — Swift app rules

Applies to everything under `app/`. Build/verification commands and the FFI
lockstep are in the root `CLAUDE.md`; the full design is
`designs/spec/` (§3–4 the UI, §7.4–7.8 the platform side; its `README.md` is
the index). The
long form of each entry below — why each file is the shape it is, and the
traps its history turned up — is `designs/adr/app-file-history.md` (the
full history, every size toll and measurement, is archived; see its
"Original" line); this file is what governs a file now. Files
are listed by family; a file with a header comment of its own carries its
detail there.

  `planJSON` are memoised PER HANDLE, so keep handles rather than minting
  them; so is `sourceMap(_:)`, `rc_project_source_map` decoded and checked
  once per handle and clip, SR-20), timecode, snapping (export presets/sizes/settings are

  `CoreValues.swift` — no Swift file types a speed bound), `ReelColor` (`rc_normalise_color`, G-25) and `ReelAgentSocket` (below);

  `ReelContainer` (`rc_container_*`, a WebM/Matroska file's index, #216-R), `ReelCube`,

  wrappers (below), with `ReelGraphicPackage` (`rc_graphic_package_write`, G-46; `read`,

  It is also where the op table is read BACK: `ReelOp.coreNames()` over

  `deinit` frees the Rust allocation. It also holds **the one read of
  `rc_project_apply`'s TWO message channels**, in the header's own order — a

- `OpDictionaries.swift` — the `dictionary` extensions on the §5.2

  `ReelCore.swift` and `ReelOps.swift`, the only files that write an op

  patch key: absent, an explicit null, or the value.
- `ReelOps.swift` — `OpArgs`, `ReelOp` and one typed factory per row of

  core's `none`: a case named `none` warns), `CursorProps` (`VideoProps.cursor` and
  `VideoPatch.cursor`; its `dictionary` writes all eight keys, `NSNull` for a nil `hideIdle`),

  under `cursor` only when `cursor` is nil, never decoded, `cutoutPart`'s shape — so each Cursor

  hide_idle) and `animatable` (the other six)), with `CursorProps.smoothingSteps`,

  `MediaCursor` (`MediaSnapshot.cursor`, `MediaDescriptor.cursor`, kept by `probeDictionary`) and

**Frozen files.** `EditorViewController.swift`, `TimelineView.swift`,
`PreviewCanvasView.swift`, `AgentServer.swift` are **frozen at current
size**: anything adding more than ~50 lines goes in an extension file
(`EditorViewController+<Feature>.swift`, `TimelineView+<Feature>.swift`,
`AgentServer+<Feature>.swift`) or a new `…SheetController`, and the frozen
file keeps only the wiring — a stored property, a closure assignment, a
validator arm, a draw call. The pieces extension files build on are therefore
internal, not private. Pitfalls: a selector declared `@objc` on an extension
needs NO forward in the frozen file (a second declaration is an error); a
command whose body sits at the foot of a non-extension feature file carries
its validator arm there too, or the item falls through to the closing
`return true`; `handleEditorCharacter`'s bare-key `switch` matches in SOURCE
order, so a bare `case "x"` goes BELOW any modified `case "x" where …`; and
`handleEditorKey` refuses while a sheet is attached, because a sheet is
window-modal and the preview panel's forwarded keys would otherwise reach
the key map behind it.

  "absent keeps": a `video.filters` entry must name both its keys, because a

  further on. `GROUPS` — every group in its order on `Clip`, the order

  ticks, which is what lets a refusal name the number the caller sent rather
  than the one a snap rounded it to. Gradient stops are deliberately NOT

## Rules

**Modules and size.** New feature area = new module with its own
`impl Project` block. Soft cap ~600 lines; needing a new `// ---- name --`
banner section is the signal to split. Every module keeps a `//!` doc;
numeric and algorithmic choices get prose "why" comments. **A file at the cap
gives something up BEFORE it takes anything on**: the cut is a PURE MOVE,
landed and gated alone, so the feature's diff is attributable; budget the cut
against the pessimistic number, because an estimate here has run about two
thirds of the truth. Over the cap today and known debt, not licence:
`edit.rs`, whose
standing exemption is that its module doc IS the op table's semantics half
(the cut there, if ever forced, is the `Op` enum into an `edit_ops.rs`, and
never in the same phase as a feature). The current list is `wc -l`; named
seams are in `designs/adr/core-file-history.md` "Named next cuts".

**Dependencies.** `serde` and `serde_json` (the JSON the FFI speaks),
`tiny_http` (the agent's socket), and `serde_path_to_error`, which is there
so a patch refusal names the path to what only the type can refuse (a
misspelt variant, a `null` a required field cannot take), where serde alone
names only the value. `graphic` (the path crate `../graphic`, road map
10's motion-graphics engine), named by `ffi_graphic.rs` alone. It enables
`serde_json`'s `preserve_order`, and a feature is unified across a path
dependency, so the core's `serde_json` has it too; `Cargo.toml` spells it
out. `svgtypes` 0.16.1 (usvg's own pin, already in the lock) for its
named-colour table only, so a stored name agrees with what usvg draws
(`model_color.rs`). `sha2` for the `.fjgraphic` manifest's checksums
(G-46; also `graphic_ffi.rs`'s revision oracle).

**One implementation per algorithm.** Before writing time math, find the
existing implementation and route through it. Shared constants have exactly
one home (`TIMESCALE` in `time.rs`; `RC_*` caps in `format.rs`; the
inspector's bounds in `props_check.rs`).

**Purity.** Every edit takes `&self` and returns a new value — internally
clone-then-mutate. An op that would change nothing returns
`Outcome::Identity`, never an identical copy: an identical copy registers a
phantom undo step in the app.

**Errors.** Every edit answers `Result<Outcome, String>` — three arms and
one tier, no error enum. `Outcome::Applied` = the new project;
`Outcome::Identity` = the op is valid and nothing needed to change;
`Outcome::Refused(String)` = a rule declined it, carrying the rule's OWN
sentence rather than a second one written at the call site; `Err(String)` =
invalid arguments, unknown ids, parse failures — lowercase messages naming
the offending value. A refusal is not an error tier: both middle arms leave
the project untouched and register no undo step. No input may panic. FFI
mapping (`ffi_edit.rs`): `Applied` → a new handle; `Identity` → NULL with
neither channel written; `Refused` → NULL with the sentence through
`reason_out`; `Err` → NULL with the message through `err_out`; caught panic
→ `"internal error: <what>"`. The two channels are never both written.

**Times.** Every tick value that reaches the model is snapped to the
document's frame grid before it is stored (`time::snap_to_frame`). Never
store a sub-frame time. Where a range check names the value, the check runs
on what the CALLER sent and the snap follows it, so a refusal never names a
number the door rounded to (`props_check.rs`, `edit_props.rs`'s
`snap_motion` / `snap_animation`). The one family that is deliberately NOT
on the grid is the audio ramps — `audio.fade_in` / `fade_out`, the duck's
and the compressor's attack and release — because they are envelope lengths
sampled at the audio rate, not positions in the picture, and quantising them
to a video frame would round a 10 ms attack to nothing. The other is a SHIFT
(spec §11 #42): an op that moves several clips — the ripples, `close_gap`,
`insert_time`, `move_clip` — moves them all by ONE delta so abutments stay
exact, and at a rate whose frame is not a whole number of ticks (7 fps) a
moved start may sit a tick off the grid; a canvas rate change re-snaps (D7-3).

**FFI exports.** Every export: `#[no_mangle] pub unsafe extern "C"`, a `///`
comment restating the header contract, a `/// # Safety` paragraph, NULL
tolerance first, narrow `unsafe {}` blocks. Route through the shared helpers
in `ffi_util.rs` — a freshly hand-rolled `catch_unwind` is a review flag.
Export names mirror the Rust method exactly.

**Format changes.** Any change to persisted project state bumps
`RC_FORMAT_VERSION` in `format.rs` **and** the `#define` in
`core/include/framejob_core.h`; the reader must keep accepting every prior
version; the writer enforces the reader's caps. A bump whose new fields all
carry a serde default needs no migrate step (versions 3 through 15 have none;
15's one step only renumbers the branch's 1015)
but still bumps, because unknown keys are ignored at every level by design
and an older build would otherwise open the file, drop the new fields on read
and write the loss back on the next save; a bump that changes a field's
SHAPE adds a step at the migration hook (`migrate_1_to_2`). Each bump gets a
`schema_vN.rs` test that opens the previous versions' fixtures and reads the
new keys' ORDER off the written text, since a parsed `Value` sorts them.
**Nothing that checks the version writes the current number as a
literal**, so a bump edits `format.rs` (and `format_history.rs`'s paragraph)
and the header and no test or proof:
- The "one past the current version, refused" tests in
  `core/tests/schema_v3.rs` and `core/tests/model_tests.rs` compute
  `RC_FORMAT_VERSION + 1` and assert the refusal's whole message with
  both numbers.
- `schema_v3.rs`'s `the_header_states_the_same_format_version_as_the_core`
  holds the header's `#define` to `format.rs`'s constant, so a bump that
  moves only one of them fails `make test`.
- The schema tests' and `model_tests.rs`'s `/version` assertions read
  `RC_FORMAT_VERSION`; `schema_v10.rs`'s byte-for-byte round trips rewrite
  the fixture's version line through its `current()` helper.
- The proof scripts (`tools/proof/*_proof.py`) read the HEADER's number
  through a `format_version()` helper. `phase9`'s "one past" fixture is
  `format_version() + 1`, and its every-version loop runs up to the current
  version. A proof that expected a literal would fail weeks later, in
  someone else's session, with nothing pointing at the bump.

A fixture's own version (`e2_proof.py`'s `VERSION = 8`, a
`schema_vN.rs`'s older files) is a literal on purpose. One claim still
moves with the schema rather than the number: when a bump appends a key to
the video object, `schema_v4.rs`'s text assertion about what follows
`obscure` fails in `make test` and names the new neighbour.

**Tests.** All tests are black-box in `core/tests/` (no `#[cfg(test)]` in
`src/`), exercised **through the FFI** wherever possible, and verified
against independently written oracles — never golden files. Shared helpers
live in `tests/common/` (`content` / `contents` — "the same clips, ids
aside" — is the one spelling of that comparison, used by `nest`'s identity
claim and `scope`'s oracle alike); new feature area = new test file. Every
new export gets at least one test plus inclusion in the null-safety sweep.
Finish Rust work with `cargo fmt` and a clean `make lint`.

19	        ", obscure (an ARRAY of {shape: rect|ellipse, x, y, width, height, feather, kind, "

35	        ", blend (how this layer combines with what is already on the canvas: "
36	        + "\(blendNames.joined(separator: "|")) — normal is source-over, which is what "
37	        + "every project drew before this key existed. A blend needs something UNDER it: "
38	        + "over the empty canvas multiply, darken and overlay read black while screen, "
39	        + "add, lighten and difference change nothing, so add_background is usually the "
40	        + "call before this one. It is forced to normal for the length of a cross "
41	        + "dissolve, whose own weighting requires it, so what the frame shows there can "
42	        + "legitimately differ from the value get_project reports)"

70	        + "meet rather than refusing. It is NOT an animation target — set_action_end "

5	/// The catalog's FILE half: the thirteen tools whose every row is about a path
6	/// on disk — the six of Media (a file probed into the list, a caption file
7	/// read onto a track, the package consolidated, and the three raw media ops),
8	/// the two of Captions (a transcript made, a caption file written), the two
9	/// of Rendering and export (a frame, the movie, and the two that follow and
10	/// stop the movie's job) and, since road map 3, the one of Recording (a
11	/// movie the app wrote itself). Three of the thirteen
12	/// are ops (`add_media`, `relink_media`, `remove_media`), so they are built
13	/// with `opTool` — their arguments PRINTED from the core's published table
14	/// (road map 7's D3) — and get a `scope` as every op does; the other ten
15	/// are app-state tools of spec §7.9 with no op behind them and nothing to
16	/// read from that table, so they declare their schemas whole through `tool`.
17	/// `record_screen` is among those, declaring NO `scope` by construction,
18	/// since `tool` injects one for the core's op names only and the parity
19	/// check's fourth part reads those. Eight of the thirteen are built elsewhere
20	/// and spliced back in at the points they left, so the order is unchanged:
21	/// `import_captions`, `transcribe` and `export_captions` in
22	/// `AgentCatalog+Captions.swift`, `render_frame`, `export`,
23	/// `export_status` and `cancel_export` in `AgentCatalog+Render.swift`, and
24	/// `record_screen` in `AgentCatalog+Recording.swift`.

27	/// app/CLAUDE.md's ~600 cap — road map 2's phase 9 had put it back over the
28	/// cut `AgentCatalog+Clips.swift` bought — and whose own header named this
29	/// cut in advance. It is road map 3's R1·toll, paid first and alone. The
30	/// seam is the one the file had drawn: `// MARK: Media`, `// MARK: Captions`
31	/// and `// MARK: Rendering and export` came here whole, in their existing
32	/// order, with their bodies untouched, and so did the hoisted locals nothing
33	/// outside them reads. Those locals left again with their rows: the caption
34	/// format's for `AgentCatalog+Captions.swift` (road map 6's C1 toll 2), and
35	/// `render_frame`'s and `export`'s five for `AgentCatalog+Render.swift`

42	/// other side and is handed in here, and on to `renderTools`. The old
43	/// header's "none of them shares a hoisted local with the groups that stay"
44	/// was false by exactly that one, and it is corrected there.
45	///
46	/// These three groups are the LAST three of the catalog, so the splice is an
47	/// append after the Canvas group and the catalog's order — the order an agent
48	/// reads the tools in — is what it always was; `tools/list` byte-identical
49	/// before and after the cut is the gate that says so. The move is about 400

51	/// this project keeps re-learning about budgeting a cut against the
52	/// pessimistic number.

128	                "Removes a media entry from the project. Media still used by clips is refused "

30	    /// taught here: `glide`, `active_fill` and `pause_dim`.
31	    static let textWordsClause: String =
32	        ", case (as_written|upper — applied before layout; it never changes the word count), "
33	        + "words (one {start, end} per whitespace token of content, in clip ticks, or [] for "
34	        + "an untimed page — a content change that alters the count must send words: [] in "
35	        + "the same patch), word_style (null or {mode: highlight|build, active_color, "
36	        + "active_scale 1–1.5, active_pill {color, padding, radius, glide}, spoken_color, "
37	        + "upcoming_color, active_fill, pause_dim 0–1} — how the word being said is drawn; it "
38	        + "replaces animation. Three looks, each off by default: active_pill.glide (true|false) "
39	        + "slides the pill from the word before to the active one over 0.2 s, or sooner when "
40	        + "the next word starts sooner, instead of jumping; active_fill (true|false) fills the "
41	        + "active word left to right from its start to its end, taking 0.6 s at most — the "
42	        + "part said in active_color and the rest in upcoming_color, or not yet drawn in build "
43	        + "mode; in highlight mode it shows only where those two colours differ; pause_dim "
44	        + "fades the words and the pill to 1 − pause_dim of their opacity in a pause of 0.25 s "
45	        + "or more — after one word's end until the next one's start, before a late first "
46	        + "word, and after the last word until the clip ends — over 0.1 s each way, and outside "
47	        + "0–1 it is refused)"

5	/// The catalog's FILE half: the thirteen tools whose every row is about a path
6	/// on disk — the six of Media (a file probed into the list, a caption file
7	/// read onto a track, the package consolidated, and the three raw media ops),
8	/// the two of Captions (a transcript made, a caption file written), the two
9	/// of Rendering and export (a frame, the movie, and the two that follow and
10	/// stop the movie's job) and, since road map 3, the one of Recording (a
11	/// movie the app wrote itself). Three of the thirteen
12	/// are ops (`add_media`, `relink_media`, `remove_media`), so they are built
13	/// with `opTool` — their arguments PRINTED from the core's published table
14	/// (road map 7's D3) — and get a `scope` as every op does; the other ten
15	/// are app-state tools of spec §7.9 with no op behind them and nothing to
16	/// read from that table, so they declare their schemas whole through `tool`.
17	/// `record_screen` is among those, declaring NO `scope` by construction,
18	/// since `tool` injects one for the core's op names only and the parity
19	/// check's fourth part reads those. Eight of the thirteen are built elsewhere
20	/// and spliced back in at the points they left, so the order is unchanged:
21	/// `import_captions`, `transcribe` and `export_captions` in
22	/// `AgentCatalog+Captions.swift`, `render_frame`, `export`,
23	/// `export_status` and `cancel_export` in `AgentCatalog+Render.swift`, and
24	/// `record_screen` in `AgentCatalog+Recording.swift`.
25	///
26	/// A pure move out of `AgentCatalog.swift`, which stood at 807 lines against
27	/// app/CLAUDE.md's ~600 cap — road map 2's phase 9 had put it back over the
28	/// cut `AgentCatalog+Clips.swift` bought — and whose own header named this
29	/// cut in advance. It is road map 3's R1·toll, paid first and alone. The
30	/// seam is the one the file had drawn: `// MARK: Media`, `// MARK: Captions`
31	/// and `// MARK: Rendering and export` came here whole, in their existing
32	/// order, with their bodies untouched, and so did the hoisted locals nothing
33	/// outside them reads. Those locals left again with their rows: the caption
34	/// format's for `AgentCatalog+Captions.swift` (road map 6's C1 toll 2), and
35	/// `render_frame`'s and `export`'s five for `AgentCatalog+Render.swift`

40	/// the clip rows take three: `render_frame`'s `t` row reads `ticks`, which
41	/// the Projects and Markers groups read as well, so `ticks` stayed on the
42	/// other side and is handed in here, and on to `renderTools`. The old
43	/// header's "none of them shares a hoisted local with the groups that stay"
44	/// was false by exactly that one, and it is corrected there.
45	///
46	/// These three groups are the LAST three of the catalog, so the splice is an
47	/// append after the Canvas group and the catalog's order — the order an agent
48	/// reads the tools in — is what it always was; `tools/list` byte-identical
49	/// before and after the cut is the gate that says so. The move is about 400
50	/// lines rather than the 300 the old header guessed, which is the warning
51	/// this project keeps re-learning about budgeting a cut against the
52	/// pessimistic number.

4	/// `set_transition_style`, road map 5 E1's ops (format version 7).
5	///
6	/// A file of its own rather than two more rows in `AgentCatalog+Clips.swift`,
7	/// which is the file the forty-five clip and action rows already live in and
8	/// is well over the size cap. The two rows are spliced into `catalogJSON()`
9	/// immediately AFTER that group — right where `set_transition` and
10	/// `set_transition_duration` end — and never appended at the very end of the
11	/// catalog, which is where `tools/proof/recording_probe.py` reads the last
12	/// eleven names from.

14	/// Both rows are `opTool`'s (road map 7's D3·4): the PROSE is here and the
15	/// structure — the two vocabularies among it — is printed from the core's
16	/// published table, so the thirteen kinds and the three alignments are the
17	/// core's own list rather than `TransitionKind.allCases` restated. `scope`
18	/// arrives on both for free: `tool()`, which `opTool` goes through, puts one
19	/// on every row whose name the CORE calls an op (`rc_op_names`), so an op
20	/// tool cannot be declared without one.
21	extension AgentServer {
22	    /// The transition rows, given the two SENTENCES the clip group already
23	    /// hoisted — the ticks note and the clip-id prose — so neither is spelled
24	    /// a second time.
25	    func transitionTools(ticks: String, clipDescription: String) -> [[String: Any]] {
26	        return [
27	            opTool(
28	                "add_transition",
29	                "Makes an overlap at the HARD CUT before a clip and puts a transition on it — "
30	                    + "Clip ▸ Transition ▸ <kind> on a clip that abuts the one before it. The "
31	                    + "overlap is built out of material the two clips already have (the source "
32	                    + "before the incoming clip's in point, and after the outgoing clip's "
33	                    + "out point), so NOTHING else on the timeline moves and the pair's outer "
34	                    + "edges stay exactly where they were. duration is snapped down to whole "
35	                    + "frames and CLAMPED — to each side's available material, to the "
36	                    + "neighbours on the track, and to the overlap rule — so a request too "
37	                    + "long for the media lands shorter rather than failing; a request that "
38	                    + "clamps below one frame is refused. An affected track already outside "
39	                    + "the overlap rule is refused by that rule before fitting. align center takes half from "
40	                    + "each side (an odd frame goes to the incoming clip, and a side with "
41	                    + "nothing to give passes its share to the other), before takes it all "
42	                    + "from the incoming clip's head, after all from the outgoing clip's tail. "
43	                    + "kind absent uses the clip's stored kind if it has one and "
44	                    + "cross_dissolve otherwise; a stored transition keeps its curve and "
45	                    + "crossfade, a new one is eased at both ends and crossfades its sound. "
46	                    + "The incoming clip's actions move with its new first frame, so a zoom "
47	                    + "stays on the source frame it was drawn over. Errors when duration is "
48	                    + "not positive and when the clip is NOT at a hard cut, naming which of: "
49	                    + "no clip before it, a gap, an overlap that already exists (use "
50	                    + "set_transition or set_transition_duration for that one). With "
51	                    + "ripple true the overlap is made by MOVING instead — the sheet's Shift "
52	                    + "Clips Left button when neither clip has footage beyond the cut: no "
53	                    + "material is read and align is ignored, and the incoming clip plus "
54	                    + "every clip at or after the cut on every unlocked track slides left by "
55	                    + "duration, so the timeline gets that much shorter and no clip's source "
56	                    + "window changes. It is capped at half the shorter of the two clips and "
57	                    + "limited to the greatest whole-frame shift that leaves every moved "
58	                    + "track inside the overlap rule, including after clips cross; a clip "
59	                    + "on another track pushed into its neighbour gets a cross_dissolve; "
60	                    + "markers do not move.",
61	                [
62	                    "clip": clipDescription,
63	                    "kind": "The transition. Absent uses the clip's stored kind, else "
64	                        + "cross_dissolve. Not nullable — set_transition clears.",
65	                    "duration": "Requested overlap length, \(ticks) Clamped, never "
66	                        + "refused for being too long.",
67	                    "align": "Which side the overlap comes out of. Default center. Ignored "
68	                        + "with ripple.",
69	                    "ripple": "Make the overlap by sliding the incoming clip and everything "
70	                        + "after it left, for two clips with no footage beyond the cut. "
71	                        + "Default false.",
72	                ]),
73	            opTool(
74	                "set_transition_style",
75	                "Sets how a transition is EASED and whether it crossfades the two clips' "

77	                    + "tab's Transition section. An absent key keeps what is there, so "

81	                    + "transition on a clip with no overlap is simply not drawn until there "
82	                    + "is one — and a clip with no transition at all gets a cross_dissolve "

86	                    + "the Crossfade Shape popup. A project written before this existed "

94	                        + "out), s_curve or minus_3db (slow start); the outgoing clip takes the "

1	import Foundation
2	
3	// MARK: - Catalog: what a tool declares that its op does not
4	
5	/// One place a tool's schema deliberately differs from its op's row in the
6	/// core's published table (`core/src/op_table.rs`, road map 7's D3).
7	///
8	/// The core says what an argument IS and the app says what it is FOR, so a
9	/// tool that takes a spelling the op has never heard of — or asks for a key
10	/// the op calls optional — is saying something the table cannot. The rule
11	/// that decides which side a fact belongs on is the ticket's amendment:
12	///
13	/// > **A bound the core REFUSES outside belongs in the op table and is
14	/// > published. A bound the core merely CLAMPS to, a null that MEANS
15	/// > something, and a bare-string shorthand are the app's — declared, with
16	/// > a reason each.**
17	///
18	/// Every row carries the op, the argument, what the app adds, and why, and
19	/// `AgentServer.opTool` emits it, so **an agent can SEE a shorthand rather
20	/// than discover it**. It takes the shape of `AgentServer.opsWithoutTools`,
21	/// the "ops that deliberately have no tool" list that has stood empty since
22	/// it was written: the bar for an entry is high, and an entry is a decision
23	/// with a reason rather than an accident.
24	struct AgentDeclaration {
25	
26	    /// What a row is about.
27	    ///
28	    /// The two plural forms exist because the shared argument vocabulary
29	    /// (`AgentServer+Arguments.swift`) reads a whole CLASS of argument the
30	    /// same way — every boolean, every clip list — and a row per op would
31	    /// be the same sentence written twelve times, which is the duplication
32	    /// this whole candidate is deleting.
33	    enum Subject {
34	        /// One op's one argument.
35	        case argument(String, of: String)
36	        /// Every argument the core publishes as this JSON type, whatever op
37	        /// it belongs to.
38	        case everyArgumentTyped(String)
39	        /// Every argument with this NAME, whatever op it belongs to.
40	        case everyArgumentNamed(String)
41	    }
42	
43	    /// What a tool says about required-ness where the core's `required`
44	    /// disagrees. Both directions exist and they are opposite mistakes: a
45	    /// null that means something must not be reachable by FORGETTING the
46	    /// key, and a default the app takes from its own state must not be made
47	    /// compulsory by the core's word.
48	    enum Requirement {
49	        /// The core's answer stands, which is every argument but eight.
50	        case theCores
51	        /// The tool asks for an argument the core calls optional.
52	        case required
53	        /// The tool does not ask for one the core requires.
54	        case optional
55	        /// The tool does not PUBLISH the argument at all: the app fills it
56	        /// from what only the app can read, and the gate refuses a
57	        /// caller's own as a stranger.
58	        case filledByTheApp
59	    }
60	
61	    let subject: Subject
62	    /// JSON types this tool accepts beyond the one the core publishes.
63	    let alsoTypes: [String]
64	    let requirement: Requirement
65	    /// Schema keys this tool adds over the core's fragment.
66	    let alsoKeys: [String: Any]
67	    /// Why, in one sentence. It is documentation and not agent-facing
68	    /// prose: what an agent needs to KNOW is in the tool's own description,
69	    /// and this is the reason the row is allowed to exist at all.
70	    let why: String
71	
72	    init(
73	        _ subject: Subject, alsoTypes: [String] = [], requirement: Requirement = .theCores,
74	        alsoKeys: [String: Any] = [:], why: String
75	    ) {
76	        self.subject = subject
77	        self.alsoTypes = alsoTypes
78	        self.requirement = requirement
79	        self.alsoKeys = alsoKeys
80	        self.why = why
81	    }
82	
83	    /// Whether this row is about `argument` of `op`, whose published JSON
84	    /// type is `type`.
85	    func covers(_ op: String, _ argument: String, type: Any?) -> Bool {
86	        switch subject {
87	        case let .argument(name, of: owner): return owner == op && name == argument
88	        case let .everyArgumentTyped(published): return (type as? String) == published
89	        case let .everyArgumentNamed(name): return name == argument
90	        }
91	    }
92	
93	    /// The core's fragment for one argument, widened by this row.
94	    ///
95	    /// A `null` added to a closed vocabulary is added to its `enum` too:
96	    /// the members are the whole of what the value may be, so a schema that
97	    /// says `["string", "null"]` and lists only the names contradicts
98	    /// itself. That is the one rule here that is not a plain overwrite, and
99	    /// it exists so the null does not cost the tool the core's member list.
100	    ///
101	    /// **`alsoKeys` is a blind merge, and the rule a row must obey is that
102	    /// it may NARROW what the core published and never relax it** — a
103	    /// `minimum` tighter than the core's is a truer promise, one looser than
104	    /// the core's is a false one, and nothing here can tell the two apart.
105	    /// All six rows that use it today NARROW — `set_speed.rate` and
106	    /// `add_speed_ramp.rate` a range, `set_canvas.fps` a floor on its items,
107	    /// three lists a `minItems` — so the rule is written down rather than
108	    /// enforced: a guard that silently dropped the key would put a row in the
109	    /// list that does nothing, which is the trap this file's one shared
110	    /// predicate exists to avoid.
111	    func applied(to fragment: [String: Any]) -> [String: Any] {
112	        var property = fragment
113	        if !alsoTypes.isEmpty, let core = property["type"] as? String {
114	            property["type"] = [core] + alsoTypes
115	            if alsoTypes.contains("null"), let members = property["enum"] as? [Any] {
116	                property["enum"] = members + [NSNull()]
117	            }
118	        }
119	        for (key, value) in alsoKeys { property[key] = value }
120	        return property
121	    }
122	}
123	
124	extension AgentServer {
125	
126	    /// Every declaration, in one list (`AgentDeclaration`'s doc has the rule
127	    /// an entry has to pass). Twenty rows over seven kinds of difference:
128	    /// two bare-string shorthands, one reading of a whole JSON kind, two
129	    /// nulls that mean something, two ranges the core clamps to rather than
130	    /// refusing, one the APP refuses outside where the core's kind is
131	    /// looser, five times the tool takes from the app what the op would
132	    /// have made the caller send or would have defaulted, and three times a

328	    /// One op tool's declared input: the core's published structure, each
329	    /// argument's prose, and this op's rows from `declarations`.
330	    ///
331	    /// The three sources meet HERE and nowhere else, which is what makes
332	    /// `opTool` a printing of the table rather than a copy of it. It walks
333	    /// the CORE's published properties, so an argument with no prose is
334	    /// emitted with the core's structure and no description, and a sentence
335	    /// whose key is not an argument at all is attached to nothing — the
336	    /// fifth part of the startup parity check complains about both
337	    /// (`AgentServer+Parity.swift`), which is why `opTool` hands it the
338	    /// prose map before calling this.
339	    static func declaredInput(
340	        of op: String, _ published: ReelOpSchema, _ prose: [String: String]
341	    ) -> (properties: [String: Any], required: [String]) {
342	        // ONE question, asked the same way everywhere below: which rows are
343	        // about this argument? The published TYPE is part of the question,
344	        // since a row may name a KIND, and it is read from the CORE's own
345	        // fragment rather than from a fragment another row has already
346	        // widened — so the answer does not depend on the order the rows are
347	        // applied in, and a `.required` row on a kind or a name cannot be
348	        // silently inert the way a `.argument`-only reading left it.
349	        func rows(about argument: String) -> [AgentDeclaration] {
350	            let fragment = published.properties[argument] as? [String: Any]
351	            return declarations.filter { $0.covers(op, argument, type: fragment?["type"]) }
352	        }
353	        var properties: [String: Any] = [:]
354	        for (argument, fragment) in published.properties
355	        where !rows(about: argument).contains(where: { $0.requirement == .filledByTheApp }) {
356	            var property = fragment as? [String: Any] ?? [:]
357	            for declaration in rows(about: argument) {
358	                property = declaration.applied(to: property)
359	            }
360	            if let sentence = prose[argument] { property["description"] = sentence }
361	            properties[argument] = property
362	        }
363	        // The core's own order, less what a row calls optional, plus what a
364	        // row asks for — so a tool's required list stays the table's reading
365	        // wherever nothing declares otherwise. The additions are read in
366	        // ARGUMENT order and not in list order, because `properties` is a
367	        // dictionary and a tool's required list may not vary per process.
368	        var required = published.required.filter { argument in
369	            !rows(about: argument).contains {
370	                $0.requirement == .optional || $0.requirement == .filledByTheApp
371	            }
372	        }
373	        for argument in properties.keys.sorted() where !required.contains(argument) {
374	            guard rows(about: argument).contains(where: { $0.requirement == .required })
375	            else { continue }
376	            required.append(argument)
377	        }
378	        return (properties, required)
379	    }
380	}

/// Every op name, in table order — a projection of [`OP_TABLE`], not a
/// second list beside it.
///
/// Re-exported by `edit.rs` under the name and path it has always had, so
/// the FFI, the tests and the app all read it exactly where they did. It is
/// kept next to [`Op`] so a mistyped op can be answered with the list
/// instead of a bare parse error — models and users both mistype op names,
/// and the alternative is a serde message written in variant-speak.
///
/// [`Op`]: crate::edit::Op
pub const OP_NAMES: [&str; OP_COUNT] = names();

/// [`OP_TABLE`]'s names, read out at compile time.
const fn names() -> [&'static str; OP_COUNT] {
    let mut names = [""; OP_COUNT];
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < OP_COUNT {
        names[i] = OP_TABLE[i].name;
        i += 1;
    }
    names
}
